The Executive Secretary of the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate, Tolulope Odunaiya, has disclosed that the Federal Government has cleared all outstanding unfunded pension liabilities inherited by the directorate since it began administering the Defined Benefit Scheme in 2013. Odunaiya revealed this on Thursday in Lagos at the directorate’s stakeholders’ engagement forum, adding that the lowest-paid pensioner under the DBS now receives N58,000 monthly, up from N6,024 in 2024. According to her, the increase in the minimum monthly payout followed the implementation of various pension increments and the harmonisation policy aimed at improving pensioners’ welfare. She added that the development had raised PTAD’s monthly pension disbursement from about N8bn to over N13bn. “When I assumed office in 2024, our lowest-earning pensioner was N6,024. For now, that particular pensioner is earning N58,000. So, I just like to deeply appreciate the President for his commitment, his compassion to the pensioners of Nigeria, whether DBS, whether CPS, but particularly our DBS pensioners,” she said. Speaking further on the cleared backlog, Odunaiya stated that the unfunded liability budget line would drop to zero in the 2027 fiscal year. “Going into the 2027 budget, that line, unfunded liability, is zero. The Federal Government will no longer need to provide funds to settle unfunded liabilities under the DBS pension scheme because this government has cleared them,” she added. The PTAD boss also announced that the directorate, in collaboration with the National Health Insurance Authority, would provide nationwide healthcare coverage for DBS pensioners, noting that PTAD would prioritise the commencement of the scheme in 2027. On digital reforms, Odunaiya said PTAD had upgraded its verification process and the Aliveness Confirmation Portal to enable retirees to complete their annual verification remotely from their homes using electronic devices, eliminating the need to visit PTAD offices. She commended the Federal Government, particularly the Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, for ensuring timely monthly pension releases, while reaffirming PTAD’s commitment to sustaining regular payments and improved service delivery. In his remarks, the Chief Commissioner of the Public Complaints Commission, Bashir Abubakar, who was represented by the Deputy Director of Investigation, Mrs Amusat Medinat, said PTAD had significantly reduced pension-related complaints through prompt grievance resolution. He added that the commission had assigned a dedicated desk officer to liaise with PTAD’s Lagos office to ensure speedy case resolution. Similarly, the Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Omolola Oloworaran, represented by the Deputy to the Zonal Head, South-West, Sarah Joseph, lauded PTAD’s digital transformation initiatives, improved service accessibility and the introduction of the health insurance scheme. Oloworaran emphasised that both agencies held complementary responsibilities in Nigeria’s pension administration system, making sustained collaboration and innovation vital to guaranteeing dignified retirement for senior citizens. The National President of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Godwin Abumisi, represented by the immediate past president of the union, Kayode Ogunbiyi, commended PTAD for clearing pension increase arrears and introducing the health scheme. He, however, urged the directorate to ensure the increments are permanently factored into monthly payouts and called for close monitoring to guarantee that all presidential security palliatives reach intended beneficiaries. During the forum, retirees were guided through the pensioners’ profile page, while PTAD officials demonstrated the Aliveness Confirmation Platform, the integrated automation system and the online complaints registration portal. Meanwhile, in a separate interview with The PUNCH, the Chairman of the Nigerian Union of Pensioners, Lagos NIPOST Chapter, Adeoye Raphael, confirmed that pensioners had witnessed significant improvements in payment regularity and welfare support in recent years. Recalling past delays where retirees waited days after month-end for their stipends, Raphael noted that recent leadership at PTAD had streamlined disbursements. “In fact, pensioners nationwide haven’t had it so good,” he said, adding that successive administrations over the past dozen years had demonstrated a friendlier disposition toward retirees. Addressing the planned N32,000 across-the-board pension increment and a proposed health insurance arrangement involving Total Health Trust, he described the flat-rate addition as a major boost for low-income retirees, noting that a pensioner earning N16,500 would experience a substantial jump once implemented. “That’s a giant leap,” he stated, while urging fellow retirees to exercise patience as occasional technical glitches or bank delays could temporarily slow payments even after funds had been released.
